title: The Odyssey Box Office: Christopher Nolan's epic collects Rs 14 crore on 2nd Saturday, crosses Rs 125 crore mark
summary: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey collected Rs. 14 crore on its second Saturday in India, taking its running total to Rs. 126.75 crore. Strong weekend spikes and a star-studded cast have pushed projections to Rs. 160–170 crore before Spider-Man's release, with a clear path to surpass Rs. 200 crore if holds in later weeks.
content:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey added Rs. 14 crore on its second Saturday, registering a 70 per cent spike from the previous day. Compared to its first Saturday, the film recorded a 45 per cent drop, a solid hold for a Hollywood release. The running cume reached Rs. 126.75 crore gross at the Indian box office.

The star-studded cast — Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Robert Pattinson and others — helped sustain strong footfalls. The Odyssey is poised to see another uptick that could take its 10-day total close to Rs. 145 crore. With an uninterrupted run until Spider-Man: Brand New Day, forecasts project a Rs. 160–170 crore tally before competition intensifies.

If the film maintains momentum in weeks three and four, it is well placed to cross the Rs. 200 crore mark in India. The Odyssey has already emerged as the highest-grossing Hollywood film of 2026 in the market.

Analysts point to Christopher Nolan's brand power in India as the key driver. Nolan has become a near-synonym for event cinema among Indian audiences: his recent films and special re-releases, including Interstellar, have generated strong demand. The Odyssey, despite not being a traditionally India-friendly genre, has benefitted from that built-in audience, leaving industry watchers to speculate about what a broader-appeal Nolan film might achieve.

Disclaimer: The box office figures, opening-day forecasts, and lifetime collection projections in this article are trade estimates compiled from commercial indicators, advance-booking trends and market sentiment. They are analytical tracking figures and not certified final collections. No representation is made about the pinpoint accuracy or completeness of these projections.
